::: {.why}
It is quoted everywhere and misdescribed almost as often, and computing it yourself from a chain settles what it is in a way no description does.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Compute VIX from an option chain and reconcile against the published level.
- State three things VIX is not, including what its level does and does not forecast.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Implement the calculation and reconcile: the variance strike from each of two expiries, interpolated to 30 days, square-rooted and annualised. Compare against the published value on the same timestamp and account for any gap.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Write the three corrections: it is a risk-neutral expectation and not a forecast, it is a variance rate expressed in volatility units so it is not the expected volatility, and it includes the variance risk premium you measured on day 274. Then check the second point numerically by comparing the square root of expected variance against the expected volatility on simulated paths.
:::
:::
